content: The test image shows a soybean plant near the soil line with wilted/dead brown leaves and apparent stem collapse at the soil line. Candidates: Rhizoctonia (dry canker at soil line), Pythium_damping_off (soft rot), Phytophthora (stem discoloration from below soil). Let me check references.

- **Pythium_damping_off**: Shows very young seedlings (cotyledon stage) with soft, water-soaked rot in moist soil conditions — doesn't match (test shows drier conditions, older plant).
- **Phytophthora**: Shows plants wilting with chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward from soil — more characteristic of wet/waterlogged conditions, unlike the sandy dry soil in the test image.

The test image shows a seedling that has collapsed specifically at the soil line in dry, sandy conditions — the classic "damping-off canker" pattern of Rhizoctonia, distinct from the water-soaked soft rot of Pythium or the upward stem discoloration of Phytophthora.
